tip: The ending -inho shrinks and softens a word: minutinho is a little minute, meaning just a quick moment.
Largar de plus a verb is a casual way to say stop doing something: larga de ser teimoso.
After a preposition use mim, not eu: pra mim means for me.
Brazilian Portuguese puts the object pronoun before the verb, even at the start: Me conta.
Fazer as pazes is a set phrase meaning to make up or make peace.
Precisar always takes de before what you need: precisar de passaporte.
The conditional ending -ria turns a question into a polite offer: aceitaria um café.
Antes de is followed by the plain infinitive, not a conjugated verb: antes de começar.
With body parts Portuguese uses the article, not a possessive: os dentes means your teeth.
A gente means we but takes a singular verb: a gente está.
The verb pôr is irregular; its command form is põe: põe a roupa.
Levar is take away from the speaker; trazer is bring toward: leva o cachorro.
Guardar means to put away or store, not to guard: guarda a louça.
Ficar here means to become, marking a change of state: ficar triste is get sad.
To talk to someone, Portuguese uses falar com, not falar a: fale com o gerente.
Dar certo is a set phrase meaning to work out or turn out fine.
Decisions go with tomar, not fazer: tomar uma decisão means to make a decision.
After quando about a future event, use the future subjunctive: quando sair is when you leave.
Preencher is to fill out a form; encher is to fill up with liquid: preencha o formulário.
In affirmative commands the pronoun attaches to the verb with a hyphen: cadastre-se.
Pela is por plus a, marking for the sake of: pela minha família.
